heading: Sec. 1-1. - How Code designated and cited.
text:
The ordinances embraced in this and the following chapters and sections shall constitute
and be designated the "Code of the City of Norfolk, Virginia, 1979," and may be so
cited. Said Code may also be cited as the "Norfolk City Code, 1979".

Charter reference—
Codification of ordinances, § 16 (note).

State Law reference—
Authority of city to codify and recodify its ordinances, Code of Virginia, § 15.1-37.3.

heading: Sec. 1-2. - Rules of construction and definitions.
text:
(a)

Generally. In the construction of this Code and of all ordinances of the city, the rules and
definitions set out in this section shall apply and be observed, unless such construction
would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the council, or unless the context
clearly requires otherwise.

(b)

And, or. The word "and" shall be read as "or" and the word "or" as "and," where the sense
requires it.

(c)

Charter. The word "Charter" shall mean the Norfolk Charter of 1918, as amended from time to
time.

(d)

City. The words "city", "the city" and "this city" shall be construed as if the words "of
Norfolk, Virginia" followed them.

(e)

Code. Whenever the term "Code" or "this Code" is used without further qualification, it
shall mean the Code of the City of Norfolk, Virginia, 1979, as designated in section 1-1. Whenever reference is made to chapters or sections by number only, and without further
qualification, the reference shall apply to the appropriate chapter or section of
this Code.

(f)

Computation of time. Whenever a notice is required to be given, or an act to be done, a certain length
of time before any proceeding shall be had, the day on which such notice is given,
or such act is done, shall be counted in computing the time, but the day on which
such proceeding is to be had shall not be counted.

(g)

Council. Wherever the term "council" or "city council" is used, it shall be construed to mean
the council of the City of Norfolk, Virginia.

(h)

Gender. A word importing the masculine gender only shall extend and be applied to females
and to firms, partnerships and corporations, as well as to males.

(i)

Number. A word importing the singular number only may extend and be applied to several persons
or things as well as to one person or thing; and a word importing the plural number
only may extend and be applied to one person or thing, as well as to several persons
or things.

(j)

Oath. The word "oath" shall be construed to include an affirmation in all cases in which,
by law, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath.

(k)

Officers, boards, etc. Whenever reference is made to a particular officer, department, board, commission
or other agency, such reference shall be construed as if followed by the words "of
the City of Norfolk, Virginia."

Any reference to any specific officer shall be deemed to include his duly authorized
deputy, agent or representative.

(l)

Person. The word "person" may extend and be applied to associations, firms, partnerships
and bodies politic and corporate as well as to individuals.

(m)

Preceding, following. The words "preceding" and "following" mean next before and next after, respectively.

(n)

State or Commonwealth. The word "state" or "commonwealth" shall be construed as if the words "of Virginia"
followed it.

(o)

State Code. References to the "State Code" or "Code of Virginia" shall mean the Code of Virginia,
1950, as amended.

(p)

Street. The word "street" shall include streets, avenues, boulevards, highways, roads, alleys,
lanes, viaducts, bridges and the approaches thereto and all other public thoroughfares
in the city, and shall mean the entire width thereof between abutting property lines.
It shall be construed to include a sidewalk or footpath.

(q)

Swear; sworn. The words "swear" and "sworn" shall be equivalent to the words "affirm" and "affirmed"
in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath.

(r)

Written; in writing. The words "written" or "in writing" shall be construed to include any representation
of words, letters or figures, whether by printing or otherwise. (Code 1958, § 1-2)

State Law reference—
Similar definitions and rules of construction applicable to state law, Code of Virginia,
§ 1-13.3 et seq.

heading: Sec. 1-3. - Catchlines of sections.
text:
The catchlines of the several sections of this Code printed in boldface type are intended
as mere catchwords to indicate the contents of the section and shall not be deemed
or taken to be titles of such sections, nor as any part of the section, nor, unless
expressly so provided, shall they be so deemed when any of such sections, including
the catchlines, are amended or reenacted. (Code 1958, § 1-4)

State Law reference—
Similar provisions as to sections of state code, Code of Virginia, § 1-13.9.
